items.t: Hisun Pharma in-licenses Xuanjing Bio siRNA platform and RGN6669
items.ms: Upfront payment of RMB10 million; development milestones up to RMB348 million and sales milestones up to RMB630 million.
items.why: The deal covers cardiovascular, metabolic and respiratory targets. It requires approval at the extraordinary general meeting on 12 November 2026.
items.src: Zhejiang Hisun Pharmaceutical announcement Lin 2026-78 via SSE (2026-10-28)

items.t: Boan Biotech licenses denosumab biosimilar BA6101 (60 mg) for Japan
items.ms: The partner gains exclusive commercialisation rights in Japan; Boan receives an upfront payment, milestones and royalties. Amounts and partner were not disclosed.
items.why: The reference product Pralia had 2025 sales in Japan of JPY45.8 billion (+8.3% year on year), per the announcement.

items.t: Ferring agrees to acquire fertility biotech Gameto
items.ms: Deal value of up to $1.3825 billion, subject to development, regulatory and commercial milestones; closing remains subject to conditions.
items.why: Gameto’s In Vitro Maturation programme is investigational in the US and not FDA-approved.

items.t: Pelthos to combine with Castle Creek Biosciences (D-Fi)
items.ms: Castle Creek holders receive 5.2 million Pelthos shares (~32.5% fully diluted), up to 5.8 million more on FDA approval of D-Fi, up to $300 million in milestones (including $50 million on specified Phase 3 endpoints) and 80% of net proceeds from any priority review voucher.
items.why: Expected to close by the end of Q1 2027, subject to Castle Creek stockholder approval.

items.t: NMPA converts Junshi toripalimab urothelial cancer indication to full approval
items.ms: Monotherapy for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma after platinum chemotherapy moved from conditional to regular approval, based mainly on the RC48-C016 study (NCT05302284).

items.t: Duality/BioNTech DYNASTY-Breast02 meets PFS primary endpoint
items.ms: At interim analysis, the trastuzumab pamirtecan (DB-1303/BNT323) arm showed a statistically significant, modest PFS improvement over chemotherapy in 541 HR+/HER2-low patients; OS is immature. ILD incidence was higher than in prior trials, mostly grade 1–2.
items.why: The company states the potential clinical benefit for this population may be relatively limited; the partners will analyse the data further.

items.t: Junshi doses first patient in Phase 3 of JS207 plus JS007 for first-line HCC
items.ms: The randomized Phase 3 compares PD-1/VEGF bispecific JS207 plus anti-CTLA-4 JS007 with toripalimab plus bevacizumab. In earlier data, ORR was 44.1% and DCR 85.3% among 34 evaluable patients.

items.t: Alphamab doses first patient in Phase 3 of JSKN033 for cervical cancer
items.ms: JSKN033 (subcutaneous HER2 bispecific ADC + PD-L1 inhibitor combination) is tested as monotherapy in recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer after platinum chemotherapy and PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.

items.t: Baicheng Pharma and related party Zhiyao Technology form joint venture Hangzhou Baijing Bio
items.ms: The joint venture has registered capital of RMB20 million: Baicheng contributes RMB14 million (70%) and Zhiyao Technology RMB6 million (30%); once established it will be a controlled subsidiary of Baicheng.
items.why: Baicheng Pharma plans to set up a new company, Hangzhou Baijing Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (provisional name), with its related party Shenzhen Zhiyao Technology. It combines Baicheng's CRO/CDMO industrialisation and clinical development experience with Zhiyao's technology in AI-driven molecular design and intelligent crystal-form and formulation development, and will handle pipeline R&D, external financing, patent licensing, asset transactions and later commercialisation. Baicheng non-independent director Jiang Yide is also a director of Zhiyao Technology, so the deal is a related-party transaction; the board approved it on 23 October 2026, and it does not need shareholder approval.

items.t: CSPC starts China phase 3 of B7-H3 ADC SYS6043 in first-line triple-negative breast cancer
items.ms: Randomised, open-label, multicentre phase 3: SYS6043 versus investigator's choice of chemotherapy as first-line treatment for unresectable recurrent or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer; the first study site has been initiated.
items.why: In a voluntary HKEX announcement, CSPC describes SYS6043 as a B7-H3-targeted antibody-drug conjugate whose linker-payload is a tetrapeptide linker conjugated to a topoisomerase I inhibitor; protease cleavage releases the payload, which has a bystander effect. The announcement says its Fc design can reduce lymphocyte uptake and lower the risk of off-target toxicity. The phase 3 has started at the first site in China, and recruitment and screening are under way. No amount was disclosed; efficacy awaits the trial results.

items.t: HUTCHMED's ex-China licence of a KRAS-EGFR conjugate to GSK closes
items.ms: $110M upfront (expected shortly); up to $1.185B in regulatory, development and commercial sales milestones; plus tiered royalties on net sales.
items.why: HUTCHMED announced that its exclusive development and licence agreement with a GSK affiliate for HMPL-A830 has closed after antitrust review and other closing conditions were met. GSK obtains worldwide rights outside mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. HMPL-A830 is an antibody-targeted therapy conjugate (ATTC) that links a small-molecule KRAS inhibitor payload to an anti-EGFR antibody; a phase 1a trial started in September 2026 (NCT07718581). HUTCHMED is responsible for global phase 1 development, and GSK for later development and commercialisation in its territory.

items.t: Zelgen receives first $10M milestone payment from AbbVie for ZG006
items.ms: A $10M near-term milestone tied to clinical-trial progress, after a $100M upfront received earlier. The agreement also includes up to $60M in near-term milestone and option-related payments, up to $1.075B in milestones, and tiered royalties.
items.why: Zelgen and AbbVie signed a global strategic collaboration and option-to-license agreement for ZG006 (alveltamig) on 30 December 2025: AbbVie obtains exclusive development and commercialisation rights outside Greater China, and Zelgen keeps Greater China. The announcement says Zelgen received the $100 million upfront at the start of the year and has now received a $10 million near-term milestone from AbbVie based on clinical-trial progress. Net sales outside Greater China carry tiered royalties from high single digits to mid-double digits.

items.t: Sino Biopharm completes enrollment in phase 3 of TSLP antibody TQC2731 for nasal polyps
items.ms: The registrational phase 3 of TQC2731 as maintenance treatment for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) has completed enrollment; a phase 3 in severe asthma is ongoing.
items.why: TQC2731, developed in-house by Sino Biopharm subsidiary Chia Tai Tianqing, is a humanised monoclonal antibody against TSLP. TSLP is an epithelium-derived upstream inflammatory signal, and the announcement argues that blocking it may regulate both type 2 and non-type 2 inflammation; existing biologics mostly target type 2 inflammation, and CRSwNP still recurs after surgery in 35%–60% of patients. The announcement calls TQC2731 the first China-developed TSLP antibody to reach phase 3. No amount was disclosed; efficacy awaits the phase 3 results.

items.t: CSPC starts China phase 1 of SYH2083, a dual LFA-1/RASP eye drop for dry eye disease
items.ms: Phase 1 (SYH2083-001): single-centre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled dose escalation evaluating the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of single and multiple doses in healthy Chinese participants.
items.why: In a voluntary HKEX announcement, CSPC describes SYH2083 eye drops as a dual inhibitor of lymphocyte function-associated antigen 1 (LFA-1) and reactive aldehyde species (RASP): it blocks the LFA-1–ICAM-1 interaction and reduces LFA-1-mediated cell adhesion while trapping reactive aldehydes. The company expects the two targets to act together and overcome limitations of single-target drugs. The phase 1 has started in China, and recruitment and screening are under way. No amount was disclosed.

items.t: Hansoh and Roche sign an ADC strategic collaboration and licence agreement
items.ms: $400M upfront plus a $110M first-anniversary payment; potential milestones of more than $15B; tiered royalties. Closing is subject to customary conditions including expiry of the HSR waiting period.
items.why: Hansoh and Roche signed on 17 October 2026. The collaboration covers a set of ADC programmes: two Hansoh preclinical ADCs and several programmes built on Hansoh's ADC platform against targets proposed by Roche. Hansoh leads early development, at the latest through completion of global phase 1a; Roche is responsible for later development outside mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, where Hansoh keeps all rights. Hansoh may opt into overseas development of up to two programmes and receive additional economics on their US commercialisation. The milestone figure is a nominal cap tied to agreed conditions; whether it is paid depends on programmes advancing.

items.t: FDA grants accelerated approval to GSK's Jemperli for MSI-H/dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer
items.ms: FDA accelerated approval of dostarlimab (Jemperli) for adults with stage II–III MSI-H/dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer, based on the phase 2 AZUR-1 trial.
items.why: GSK disclosed in a Form 6-K filed with the SEC that the FDA approved Jemperli under the accelerated approval pathway for stage II–III MSI-H/dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer, which the company calls the first immunotherapy approved in this indication. In AZUR-1 the investigator-assessed 12-month sustained clinical complete response rate was 68% (98/144); the independent central review data for the primary objective are still maturing (47%, 54/116). With median follow-up of more than two years, no recurrences were reported among responders. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 20% of patients. The approval means some patients may avoid chemotherapy, radiotherapy and surgery, but it requires biomarker testing at diagnosis.

items.t: Estuary Bio raises $103M to advance local AAV therapy for ADPKD
items.ms: $93M Series A led by RA Capital plus a $10M seed co-led by 4BIO and GV; $103M in total
items.why: Estuary is developing local AAV gene therapy for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, from the Somlo and Caplan labs at Yale. EST-201 targets PKD2 and is slated for the clinic in 2027; EST-101 targets PKD1 and is slated for 2028. The $103 million total comprises a $93 million Series A led by RA Capital and a $10 million seed co-led by 4BIO and GV.

items.t: AstraZeneca and insitro form a strategic collaboration in difficult-to-treat cardiometabolic disease
items.ms: $40M upfront; up to about $1.46B in milestones; single-digit royalties; AstraZeneca takes exclusive worldwide rights to selected programmes
items.why: The collaboration covers metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies and runs on insitro's Virtual Human platform. AstraZeneca pays $40 million up front, with up to about $1.46 billion in milestones and single-digit royalties, and takes exclusive worldwide rights to selected programmes. The milestone figure is a nominal cap tied to agreed conditions, not a valuation or expected revenue; everything beyond the upfront depends on programmes advancing.

items.t: OMass Therapeutics raises a $310M Series C
items.ms: $310M (GBP230M) Series C, co-led by Bain Capital Life Sciences, Forbion and Novo Holdings
items.why: The round funds a small-molecule portfolio in endocrinology and immunology: it will take OMS1620, an MC2R antagonist, through phase 2 development in congenital adrenal hyperplasia and ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome, and generate initial clinical data for an SLC15A4 inhibitor for lupus. The $310 million (GBP230 million) financing was co-led by Bain Capital Life Sciences, Forbion and Novo Holdings.

items.t: City Therapeutics prices upsized IPO at about $200M
items.ms: 11,111,111 shares at $18 for about $200M; expected to begin trading on Nasdaq as CTY on Oct 16, closing expected Oct 19
items.why: The company sold 11,111,111 shares at $18 each for roughly $200 million in an upsized offering. The stock was expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under CTY on 16 October 2026, with closing expected on 19 October. The announcement names CITY-FXI, CITY-RBP4 and CITY-TFR2 among its programmes.

items.t: CSPC announces China IND for SYS6088, a PD-1/VEGFA/CTLA-4 trispecific
items.ms: NMPA clinical trial approval in advanced or metastatic solid tumours; PD-1/VEGFA/CTLA-4 trispecific antibody with an engineered Fc
items.why: CSPC's voluntary HKEX announcement describes SYS6088 as a PD-1/VEGFA/CTLA-4 trispecific antibody with an engineered Fc, and says China's NMPA has approved it for clinical trials in advanced or metastatic solid tumours. No deal value is attached; clinical benefit will depend on trial data still to come.

items.t: Eton licenses US rights to Aquestive's Libervant (diazepam buccal film)
items.ms: $10M upfront; up to $47.5M in milestones; mid-teens royalties; agreement dated 2026-10-13
items.why: The agreement, dated 13 October 2026 and filed by Eton on Form 8-K, gives Eton exclusive US rights to Libervant (diazepam buccal film). Terms are $10 million up front, up to $47.5 million in milestones and mid-teens royalties. Launch is set for April 2027 subject to FDA action: VALTOCO's orphan-drug exclusivity expires on 10 January 2027, and the PDUFA date for ages 6-11 is 29 March 2027.
items.src: Eton and Aquestive press release via GlobeNewswire (2026-10-14); Eton Form 8-K

items.t: Hiteck licenses next-generation NGF eye drop HT006.2.2 to Visara outside Greater China
items.ms: $7M in upfront and near-term payments; up to $104M in milestones; plus royalties; territory is outside Greater China
items.why: Hiteck (300683) out-licenses its investigational next-generation nerve growth factor eye drop HT006.2.2 to Visara for neurotrophic keratitis outside Greater China; Visara is a majority-owned subsidiary of NovaBridge (NBP) and runs the asset as VIS-102. Terms are $7 million in upfront and near-term payments, up to $104 million in milestones, and royalties. In a phase 1b study in Chinese subjects with severe NK, 50% of the highest-dose cohort achieved complete corneal healing after a single 8-week course, compared with 14% on vehicle at week 4.
items.src: Hiteck announcement via cninfo (2026-10-13); PR Newswire release

items.t: MicuRx licenses MRX-23 ADC and grants STOPIN platform options to ClearideBio
items.ms: $1M non-refundable upfront; MRX-23 milestones capped at a nominal $223M; options on up to 6 STOPIN programs at up to $125M each ($750M if all are exercised); plus sublicensing revenue share or sales royalties
items.why: MRX-23 is an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) candidate from MicuRx; its target and indication were not disclosed. ClearideBio Therapeutics AG (Switzerland) takes exclusive worldwide rights to develop, manufacture and commercialize it across indications. Separately, ClearideBio receives options on up to six targets or target combinations from MicuRx's STOPIN ADC platform, built around a novel camptothecin payload; platform rights vest only after an option is exercised and an exercise fee is paid, while MicuRx keeps the platform's core intellectual property. Headline milestone caps are theoretical maxima, not a valuation or expected revenue, and everything beyond the non-refundable upfront depends on options and milestones being reached. With $1 million paid up front against up to $973 million in headline milestones, this is an option-heavy bet on an unproven payload platform by a Swiss licensee, not a conventional China out-licensing payday.
items.src: Fineline Cube (2026-10-10), reporting MicuRx's SSE announcement

items.t: Asieris grants Theramex exclusive rights to APL-1702 (CEVIRA) in Europe and other markets
items.ms: $15M upfront + $11M near-term regulatory milestone + commercial milestones and tiered sales royalties; subject to conditions precedent
items.why: APL-1702 (CEVIRA) is a photodynamic drug-device for HPV-related cervical precancerous lesions, including CIN. It combines local drug delivery with controlled light activation in an integrated intravaginal device that a clinician fits in the office and the patient removes at home, and is positioned as a non-surgical, tissue-sparing option for women who would otherwise be considered for surgery. China's NMPA approved CEVIRA in March 2026 as a first-in-class non-invasive therapy for cervical precancerous lesions; in Europe it remains investigational. Theramex, a London-based women's health company operating in more than 50 countries, gets exclusive rights in all European countries plus Australia, New Zealand and Turkey, and Asieris keeps the rest of the world. Even the upfront is conditional on a supply agreement, successful manufacturing-site audits, alignment with the upstream licence and a clarification with the European Commission on how the device's clinical value will be assessed. The deal is a bet that an office-based, non-surgical option can win over European regulators and payers; no EU approval has been announced.
items.src: Asieris press release via PR Newswire (2026-10-07)
